newsitem.title: USA: Flooding from Fran kills two in West Virginia.
newsitem.headline: Flooding from Fran kills two in West Virginia.

text.p: At least two people died and 12 West Virginia counties were declared disaster areas on Friday as rain from Hurricane Fran sent rivers over their banks in the eastern part of the state, emergency officials said.
Several residents evacuated their homes but officials could not provide exact numbers. Scattered power outages were reported across the state.
A 19-year-old man drowned in a creek in Pendleton County, state police said. An emergency dispatcher said a second person died in Grant County when his vehicle was swept away by floodwaters.
West Virginia Governor Gaston Caperton declared 12 counties disaster areas because of the high waters. Most of the counties are in the state's eastern panhandle.
Pendleton County appeared to be hit the hardest, with most major roads closed due to high water and debris. State police rescued a man there whose pickup truck was trapped in high water.
Friday's flooding marks the fourth time this year that West Virginia has been hit by serious flooding.
National Weather Service officials said some areas received more than a foot of rain on Friday. Saturday's forecast called for diminishing rainshowers and partly cloudy skies in most of the state.
